title: Project limitation — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, a cloud deployment was not executed. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud that the cloud deployment was not executed, and say what that leaves unproven, without apologising for it.

vocabulary.meaning: a boundary of your own work stated before anyone asks, which makes the rest of the report credible
the specific action that would remove a limitation, which turns an admission into a plan

expectedElements: The unexecuted step is stated plainly and early
What remains unproven is bounded, not vague
modelAnswer: I should say up front that the cloud deployment was not executed. What that leaves unproven is specific: whether the provider accepts our definition, whether the quotas allow the shape we asked for, and whether the network rules behave as written. Everything else in the report was run and recorded, and that evidence stands. I am not going to soften that, because if I let it pass as done, every other claim in the report becomes suspect. The next experiment is one run against a temporary subscription, which would settle all three questions in a day. I can schedule it as soon as we have access.
commonMistakes: Placing the limitation at the end where it reads as an afterthought
Stating the limitation vaguely so the reader cannot tell what is unproven
variants: Answer again when the interviewer treats the gap as disqualifying.
